cohort: The study included 63 pregnant women with known or newly diagnosed cardiac disease who delivered between 2011-2023 in three university departments of Obstetrics and Gynecology in Thessaloniki, Greece.
finding: The study found a tendency towards cesarean delivery in women with cardiac disease in Northern Greece, often without being strictly necessitated by national and European guidelines.
mod_finding: Out of the total sample, 36.5% underwent vaginal delivery and 63.5% underwent cesarean delivery; among those with cesarean sections due to cardiac disease, 82% could have potentially attempted vaginal delivery according to guidelines.
